reference: No GNU/POSIX sshd command implements this Bash builtin's command-stream server contract, so operation parity would be misleading. The runnable contract cases use Bash's documented type/help builtin behavior; expected builtin kind and synopsis come from Bash metadata semantics and the sshd short_doc/sshd_doc entries in loadables/sshd.c. Server operations are deferred with their required isolated protocol, key, or process references stated explicitly.
coverage: Bash reports sshd as an enabled builtin through type -t.
Bash help -s exposes the documented sshd synopsis.
Bash help -d exposes the short description registered for sshd.
Deferred native and encrypted listener interoperability, host-key lifecycle, configuration and authorization policy, session lifecycle, and SFTP/forwarding behavior.
exclusions: There is no matching GNU/POSIX CLI for this native Bash server; OpenSSH sshd is a different implementation and protocol surface, so it is not used as a fake parity oracle.

No sshd operation was invoked. Listener setup, authentication, user/account interaction, key generation, session signaling, SFTP, and forwarding require future disposable fixtures or mocks and are deferred by the task's safety limits.

cases.purpose: Verify Bash resolves the registered sshd command as a builtin, using the documented type -t result.
Verify help -s reports the short synopsis registered for sshd; expected text is the sshd_struct short_doc in the published source.
Verify help -d exposes the documented short description registered in sshd_doc[0].
Exercise sshd keygen, explicit missing-key refusal, and lazy native/encrypted host-key creation and permissions.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r2: Native key creation, mode and public file are checked, but the documented placeholder bytes are not asserted.; r4: Lazy native creation and notice pass. The encrypted-key case used a scan parser that included a comment line, so its key-equality observation is invalid pending correction and rerun.

cases.purpose: Check the native framed loopback protocol, --once behavior, stdin/stdout/stderr streaming, remote exit status, and session recording.
Check encrypted SSH key exchange and public-key authentication against an independent SSH client using generated test-only keys.

cases.purpose: Check sshd -F parsing for supported directives, Include expansion, Match blocks, invalid values, and configuration reload behavior.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: The shared fixture exercises listen address/port, host key, authorized keys, password-disabled and forwarding policy. PubkeyAuthentication disable and a positive AllowAgentForwarding channel still need explicit assertions.; r2: Absolute Include glob expansion and exclusion of nonmatching files pass. Relative-to-parent expansion in the reviewed contract remains untested; OpenSSH resolves relative Includes differently.; r3: Matching/nonmatching Address blocks exercise PermitTTY. Match User/All and PermitRootLogin/forwarding overrides remain untested.; r5: Not executed.

cases.purpose: Check authorized-key matching and restrictions, password-auth policy, forced commands, accepted environment variables, root-login policy, and forwarding authorization.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r2: The from, no-pty and no-port-forwarding restrictions are exercised. The per-key no-agent-forwarding branch remains untested.; r4: Requires the bash-os kernel auth device /dev/bashos-auth (sshd.c:165,2160-2185) used to verify the PHC hash; the Debian trixie VM kernel has no such device, and a script cannot emulate a kernel ioctl interface.; r7: Not executed (sshd.c:2950-2965).; r8: Direct forwarding allow/deny is exercised; the allowed round-trip exposes a candidate lost-reply defect. Reverse-forward authorization denial remains untested.
